title: Fix for the false virus warning
summary: Some browsers and antivirus programs wrongly called the PlazCode download a virus. This update removes the things in the PlazCode app that made it look suspicious to them.
improved: The PlazCode app now carries standard Windows program details (company name, copyright and a proper application manifest), like most normal programs.
fixed: Chrome and some antivirus programs flagged the 1.24.22 download as a virus. It was a false alarm: PlazCode is not malware.

When the AI runs a PowerShell command, PlazCode now uses a normal script file instead of a scrambled command line, and no longer turns off PowerShell's safety setting. These two things are what real malware often does, so scanners were suspicious.
Links and Obsidian notes now open the normal Windows way instead of through an old Windows helper that scanners also watch for.
Updates and add-on setup no longer switch off PowerShell's safety setting either.
notes: Everything works the same as before: commands, updates, links and add-ons.
A brand-new unsigned app can still be flagged until it builds up a good reputation; code signing is the full cure.
The Windows app is unsigned and the Mac app is not notarized, as before. Your computer may ask you to confirm opening it.

sections.title: 🛠️ What's fixed
items: Chrome and some antivirus programs called the 1.24.22 download a virus. It was a false alarm.
PowerShell commands from the AI now run as a normal script file instead of a scrambled command line, and PowerShell's safety setting stays on.
Links and Obsidian notes open the normal Windows way.
Updates and add-on setup keep PowerShell's safety setting on too.
The app now has standard Windows program details (company, copyright, manifest).

sections.title: 🧪 What was checked
items: Full tests passed on Windows, Mac and Linux, including the Mac app.
A new check confirms the Windows app no longer contains any of the patterns scanners flagged.
Commands, updates, links and add-ons work as before.
The Windows app is unsigned and the Mac app is not notarized, as before. A new unsigned app can still be flagged until it builds a reputation.
